name: Web product
description: A TypeScript application with authentication, charts, email and a local SQL dependency.

components.name: Next.js + TypeScript
components.instructions: Use the App Router and TypeScript. Keep credentials and service SDK calls on the server. Match the existing package manager; select compatible releases and commit the lockfile.
checks: Type checking, production build and a page smoke test pass.

components.name: Better Auth
components.instructions: Use the official Next.js integration. Choose a supported SQL adapter and migrations. Define session, origin, verification and password-reset policies explicitly.
checks: Test sign-in, sign-out, expired sessions and authorization boundaries.
Test verification/reset flows using a fake email sender.

components.name: PostgreSQL
components.instructions: Use migrations and a connection pool. Select a supported release and pin the deployment image digest. Document backup and restoration; do not expose the database to the public network. The supplied Compose volume layout targets PostgreSQL 17; choose a reviewed 17.x image tag or digest. Review data-directory and migration changes before using another major.

env.name: POSTGRES_IMAGE
env.purpose: Reviewed PostgreSQL 17 image tag or digest, compatible with the supplied volume layout.

env.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env.purpose: Local database password supplied outside the template.

checks: Migrate a fresh database and test backup restoration.

components.name: Apache ECharts
components.instructions: Use ECharts for charts; load browser-dependent code on the client. Provide accessible labels or a tabular alternative, responsive sizing and empty/loading/error states.
checks: Charts resize correctly and handle empty, large and invalid data.

components.name: Resend
components.instructions: Use the official server-side SDK through a small application email adapter. Verify the sending domain, handle API errors and retries, and keep real sends outside automated tests.

env.name: RESEND_API_KEY
env.purpose: Server-only Resend API key; never place it in browser code.

checks: Test adapter behavior with mocked delivery, including failure and duplicate requests.

components.name: Docker Compose
components.instructions: Use Compose for local dependencies, with health checks, named volumes and loopback-only port publishing. The included database Compose file is optional scaffolding; review image and secret references before starting it.
checks: Validate docker compose config after supplying required environment variables.
Document startup, migration, shutdown and volume/backup behavior.

decisions: Use existing conventions where they do not conflict with the chosen baseline.
Review exact dependency versions and licenses before installation.
Treat these as design starting points, not audited production deployments.

files.compose.yaml:
# Optional local database baseline. Supply values in an ignored environment file.
services:
  db:
    image: ${POSTGRES_IMAGE:?Choose a reviewed PostgreSQL 17 image tag or digest}
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: {{project_name}}
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?Set a private local database password}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U app -d {{project_name}}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
volumes:
  db-data:
